convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in MT5 indicators (iMA, iRSI). Simple entry/exit rules with fixed lot sizing. No external .mqh libraries for trading logic—Trade.mqh is standard MQL5. Single timeframe, market orders, no grid/martingale.

derived_values.name: P - pip multiplier for digit adjustment
stopLevelPips - broker minimum stop level in pips

other_exits: Long position closed when Close[1] > Fast SMA[1]
Short position closed when Close[1] < Fast SMA[1]

custom_logic_notes: Connors RSI2 strategy: Long when RSI(2) dips below 6 while price is above 200 SMA (pullback in uptrend), exit long when price closes above 5 SMA (short-term strength returns). Short when RSI(2) rises above 95 while price is below 200 SMA (bounce in downtrend), exit short when price closes below 5 SMA. Entry uses bar[1] (previous completed bar) for signal evaluation but executes at current ask/bid tick prices. Sell entry incorrectly uses currentAsk instead of currentBid for order price (line 221). Exit logic evaluates every tick with no new-bar guard, so exit signal fires on every tick while condition holds but PositionClose only succeeds once. Stop level floor ensures SL/TP respect broker minimum distances.
python_conversion_notes: 1) Digit adjustment: P=10 for 5/3/1-digit symbols, P=1 otherwise. All SL/TP must multiply by P*_Point. 2) Signal uses previous bar (index [1]) values only—implement new-bar detection for correct signal timing to avoid repeated evaluation. 3) Exit conditions are checked on every tick; in Python backtesting, evaluate exit at each bar close to match typical backtest behavior. 4) Entry price: long=ask, short=bid (note: original code has a bug using ask for sell entry). 5) Position gate: only enters when no position exists for the symbol (flat-only). 6) Stop level floor: SL and TP pips must be >= (stops_level + spread) / P to respect broker constraints. 7) RSI thresholds are asymmetric: long entry at RSI<6, short entry at RSI>95.
